diagrams.title: Op-amp gain with a finite open-loop gain
diagrams.cap: With an ideal op-amp the inverting gain is −R<sub>f</sub>/R₁. A finite open-loop gain A₀ divides it by 1 + (1 + R<sub>f</sub>/R₁)/A₀; the error is small only when the loop gain A₀·R₁/(R₁ + R<sub>f</sub>) is large.

diagrams.title: Op-amp summing, difference, integrator and differentiator
diagrams.cap: With negative feedback the inverting input sits at virtual ground, so every input element turns its voltage into a current and the feedback element turns the total back into v<sub>o</sub>: resistors add and scale, a feedback capacitor integrates, and an input capacitor differentiates.
diagrams.qq: Inverting summer, Rf = 20k, R₁ = R₂ = 10k, inputs 1 V and 0.5 V. vo?

diagrams.title: Schmitt trigger, relaxation oscillator and precision rectifier
diagrams.cap: Positive feedback gives the Schmitt trigger two thresholds ±βV<sub>sat</sub>; adding an RC from the output to the inverting input makes it oscillate with T = 2RC ln[(1 + β)/(1 − β)]. Putting a diode inside the feedback loop divides its drop by the open-loop gain, so the circuit rectifies even millivolt signals.
diagrams.qq: Inverting Schmitt, ±15 V, R₁ = R₂. Thresholds?

diagrams.title: Sallen–Key filter, Wien-bridge oscillator and the 555 astable
diagrams.cap: An equal-component Sallen–Key stage is a second-order filter whose Q is set by the amplifier gain, Q = 1/(3 − K). A Wien bridge returns one third of the output at zero phase at f = 1/(2πRC), so it oscillates with a gain of 3. A 555 astable charges C through R<sub>A</sub> + R<sub>B</sub> and discharges it through R<sub>B</sub> between V<sub>CC</sub>/3 and 2V<sub>CC</sub>/3.
diagrams.qq: Wien bridge with R₁ = 10 kΩ. Rf for oscillation?

diagrams.title: Op-amp inverting and non-inverting amplifiers
diagrams.cap: Virtual short: V₊ = V₋. Inverting input impedance = R₁; non-inverting input impedance ≈ ∞. Follower: R<sub>f</sub> = 0 → A = 1.

keys.title: Key formula explained — Op-amp gain
fields: With an ideal op-amp both inputs sit at the same voltage (virtual short), so the gain depends only on the resistors.

Tip: Positive feedback.

formulas.name: RC phase shift oscillator
notes: Where: R in Ω, C in F (three equal RC sections); A = amplifier gain
Tip: 3 RC sections × 60° = 180°.

formulas.name: Wien bridge oscillator
notes: Where: R in Ω, C in F (equal arms); A = amplifier gain
Tip: Audio frequencies.
Example: R = 16 kΩ, C = 10 nF: f = 1/(2π × 1.6 × 10⁻⁴) ≈ 995 Hz; gain 3 → Rf = 2R₁ (20 kΩ with 10 kΩ).
GATE PYQ: 2014-1 Q22

formulas.name: Colpitts
notes: Where: L = tank inductance (H), C₁, C₂ = tank capacitors (F)
Tip: Colpitts → Capacitive divider.
Example: L = 100 µH, C₁ = C₂ = 2 nF: Ceq = 1 nF → f = 1/(2π√(10⁻¹³)) ≈ 503 kHz.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: ESE 2026 Q150

formulas.name: Hartley
notes: Where: L₁, L₂ = tank inductances, M = mutual inductance (H), C = tank capacitor (F)
Tip: Hartley → Henry (inductive) divider. Crystal → most stable.

formulas.name: Ideal op-amp
notes: Where: A = open-loop gain, R<sub>in</sub>, R<sub>out</sub> = input and output resistance, BW = bandwidth, CMRR = common-mode rejection ratio
Tip: Virtual short: V<sub>+</sub> = V<sub>−</sub>.
Example: Real op-amp A = 2 × 10⁵: for 10 V out the input difference is only 10/(2 × 10⁵) = 50 µV — that is why V+ ≈ V−.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: ESE 2026 Q1 · APGENCO 2012 Q66

formulas.name: Op-amp amplifiers
notes: Where: R<sub>f</sub> = feedback resistor, R₁ = input resistor (Ω)
Example: R1 = 10 kΩ, Rf = 100 kΩ, input 0.3 V: inverting gain −10 → −3 V; non-inverting gain 11 → 3.3 V; follower → 0.3 V.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC 09/25 Q93

formulas.name: Summing & difference
notes: Where: R<sub>f</sub> = feedback resistor, R₁, R₂ = input resistors (equal pairs for the difference amplifier)
Example: Summing, all 10 kΩ, V1 = 1 V, V2 = 2 V: Vo = −3 V. Difference with Rf/R1 = 5: Vo = 5 × (2 − 1) = 5 V.

formulas.name: Integrator & differentiator
notes: Where: R in Ω, C in F, V<sub>in</sub> = input voltage
Tip: Integrator = low-pass; differentiator = high-pass.
Example: Integrator R = 10 kΩ, C = 0.1 µF (RC = 1 ms), +2 V step: Vo falls 2 V/ms → −10 V after 5 ms. Differentiator RC = 1 ms, input ramp 5 V/ms: Vo = −5 V.

formulas.name: CMRR & slew rate
notes: Where: A<sub>d</sub> = differential gain, A<sub>c</sub> = common-mode gain; SR in V/s, f = signal frequency, V<sub>m</sub> = output peak
Tip: Gain × bandwidth = constant (GBW).
Example: Ad = 2000, Ac = 0.2: CMRR = 10⁴ = 80 dB. 10 V peak at 20 kHz needs SR ≥ 2π × 20000 × 10 ≈ 1.26 V/µs.
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC PG Q171 · ESE 2026 Q2 · APGENCO 2012 Q63

formulas.name: 555 timer
notes: Where: R<sub>A</sub>, R<sub>B</sub> = timing resistors (Ω), C = timing capacitor (F), D = duty cycle
Tip: Thresholds at ⅓ and ⅔ V<sub>CC</sub>.
Example: RA = 2 kΩ, RB = 4 kΩ, C = 0.1 µF: f = 1.44/(10 kΩ × 0.1 µF) = 1.44 kHz, D = 6/10 = 60%. Monostable 10 kΩ, 1 µF → 11 ms.
GATE PYQ: 2007 Q.58
TNPSC / ESE / APGENCO PYQ: TNPSC 04/26 Q121

mistakes.c: Feedback holds it at ground potential, but no current flows into it.

mistakes.c: It is limited by the supply rails (saturation) and by the slew rate.

mistakes.c: Wien bridge needs 3; the three-section RC phase-shift oscillator needs 29.
